scenario.title: Privacy, telemetry and local-machine authority
situations: A tool call receives a privacy refusal or advisory.
A user asks what Yoke records or where data goes.
An operator needs credentials or personal files without leaking them into chat.
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
questions: Trace actual redaction at each UI/CLI/packet boundary separately; doc assertions do not prove it.
Where should the human-facing privacy/support explanation be linked before a guard fires?

lessons.title: Know who decides local-machine access
lessons.need: System privacy database reads are refused by Yoke; broad home discovery is advisory. Personal-folder reads and GUI automation remain subject to harness permissions and OS controls. Automated-test isolation is stricter than live policy.
lessons.surface: Local privacy guard diagnosis names authority and a recovery step.
lessons.gap: The refusal teaching is concrete; proactive human help entry and end-to-end delivery outside project context were not traced.

lessons.title: Distinguish Yoke telemetry from customer domain data
lessons.when: Explaining collection, retention or investigating event data
lessons.need: Read the product telemetry contract and destination. Do not generalize Yoke analytics rules to an application event store installed or built in a customer project. Data provenance, actor attribution and query-time linkage need accurate audience-specific explanation.
lessons.surface: Public Events article describes universe-local collectors, redaction, attribution and visitor links; sidebar makes article reachable.
lessons.gap: No full privacy/data-flow audit was performed. Reconcile the broad no-personal-data wording with documented actor/browser linkage rather than repeat an unchecked blanket claim.

lessons.title: Keep secrets out of explanatory output
lessons.when: Presenting command output, setup recovery or capability evidence
lessons.need: Use redacted settings/key-presence evidence and secret input channels; never dump raw config/tokens. Human browser authorization and agent explanation should expose only the data required to continue.
lessons.surface: Standing AGENTS rule -> capability/delivery home; secret-versus-settings CLI refusal.
